{{about||the English antiquarian|John Loveday (antiquary)|the New Zealand rugby union player|John Loveday (rugby player)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}'''John Stephen Loveday''' is an experimental physicist working in high pressure research. He was educated at [[Coopers School]]{{citation needed|date=September 2012}} in [[Chislehurst]] and at the [[University of Bristol]], from where he took his PhD in Physics. He currently works as a Reader in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Edinburgh]], [[Scotland]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ph.ed.ac.uk/~jsl | title=John Loveday's home page}}</ref><ref name="RSC">{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1039/B704740A|pmid = 18259632|title = High-pressure gas hydrates|journal = Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.|volume = 10|issue = 7|pages = 937–950|year = 2008|last1 = Loveday|first1 = J. S.|last2 = Nelmes|first2 = R. J.|bibcode = 2008PCCP...10..937L|hdl = 1842/3987|hdl-access = free}}</ref>

Loveday is considered one of the pioneers of [[neutron diffraction]] at high pressure{{citation needed|date=September 2012}} and was a founder member of the Paris–Edinburgh high-pressure neutron diffraction collaboration. His specialism is in techniques for high-pressure neutron scattering and examining the application of these techniques for investigating structures and transitions in planetary ices, hydrates, water and other simple molecular systems.  He is the author of more than seventy papers and his work on the behaviour of [[clathrate hydrates]] at high pressure and their relevance to models of planetary bodies including [[Titan (moon)|Titan]] was published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and has been highly cited.<ref name="RSC" /><ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1038/35070513|pmid = 11287946|title = Stable methane hydrate above 2 GPa and the source of Titan's atmospheric methane|journal = Nature|volume = 410|issue = 6829|pages = 661–663|year = 2001|last1 = Loveday|first1 = J. S.|last2 = Nelmes|first2 = R. J.|last3 = Guthrie|first3 = M.|last4 = Belmonte|first4 = S. A.|last5 = Allan|first5 = D. R.|last6 = Klug|first6 = D. D.|last7 = Tse|first7 = J. S.|last8 = Handa|first8 = Y. P.|s2cid = 4416755}}</ref>

In 2004 he helped establish the Centre for Science at Extreme Conditions,{{citation needed|date=September 2012}} where he works with Andrew D. Huxley and [[Paul Attfield]].{{citation needed|date=September 2012}}
